# BigQuery's documentation allows casting a RANGE to STRING without showing the text. GoogleSQL
# writes "[start, end)" with each bound cast to STRING and UNBOUNDED for a missing one.

SELECT CAST(RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, UNBOUNDED)' AS STRING)
?>

SELECT CAST(RANGE<DATETIME> '[UNBOUNDED, 2021-01-01 12:30:00)' AS STRING)
?>

SELECT CAST(RANGE<TIMESTAMP> '[2020-01-01 01:02:03.5+00, 2021-01-01 00:00:00+00)' AS STRING)
?>

# A RANGE<TIMESTAMP> result without formatOptions.useInt64Timestamp: whether its bounds are
# decimal seconds, as a TIMESTAMP cell's are, or microseconds.
SELECT RANGE<TIMESTAMP> '[2020-01-01 00:00:00.5+00, UNBOUNDED)'
?>

# BigQuery's message for a RANGE whose start does not precede its end, and for RANGE_INTERSECT of
# ranges that do not overlap.
SELECT RANGE(DATE '2022-12-31', DATE '2022-12-01')
?>

SELECT RANGE_INTERSECT(RANGE<DATE> '[2020-02-01, 2020-09-01)', RANGE<DATE> '[2021-06-15, UNBOUNDED)')
?>
